newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch lower, continues correctio.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch lower, continues correctio.

text.p: Nearby white sugar futures moved just lower in thin trade on Friday as the market continued its downward correction but spot August was still supported by seasonal tightness, traders said.

A trade house cross on August/October accounted for nearly half of the session volume by 1130 GMT. Little interest was reported otherwise in the spread, which was valued at around $9.00 and bid at $9.50, they said.
While August is still well supported at around $322, market sources said the spot price was seeing more sell orders close to this week's high of $330.80 to cap gains.
"There's more scale-up selling around than before, with people taking profits and trying to sell it around the $330 highs," said one.
August was down 40 cents at $326.30 and October down 10 cents at $317.20. Volume totalled a light 202 lots.
Technical analysts said the market was looking overbought so a downward correction could be on the cards. After the $330.80 high, the next upside objective was $333.50 followed by $341.00, they said.
In physical news, Iraq agreed to buy 37,500 tonnes of sugar from Egypt at a price of $14 million but the shipment will still have to be cleared by the U.N.
Pakistan cancelled its tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of white refined crystal sugar for delivery at Karachi or Port Qasim by July 31.

Russia is to buy 3.25 million tonnes of Cuban raw sugar in 1997 in exchange for sending Havana 9.75 million tonnes of Russian crude oil. Suppliers of goods under the barter deal will be selected through a tender.
Trading in Paris was confined to just 31 lots of August, down 70 cents at $326.00.
